samples.summary: Recovery creates the offline copy with `createDocument({title, type})`, which omits the `workspaceId` the backend requires — so "Save a copy" always fails with a 400
samples.evidence: `recoverOfflineCopy` calls `createDocument({ title, type: source.type })` (line 210, and `{title, type:"note"}` at line 196). `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:11-25` POSTs that payload verbatim to `${API}/documents`, which is `@Post('documents')` in `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:197` bound to `CreateDocumentInWorkspaceDto`. That DTO declares `@IsUUID() workspaceId: string` with **no** `@IsOptional()` (`packages/backend/src/document/document.dto.ts:84-85`), and `main.ts:73-79` installs a global `ValidationPipe({whitelist:true, forbidNonWhitelisted:true})`. A request with no `workspaceId` is therefore rejected with 400; `assertOk` throws, `recoverOfflineCopy` rejects, and `offline-runtime.tsx:285-288` swallows it into `toast.error('Could not recover those changes')`. The payoff path of the whole feature — handing back work the SDK could not reconcile — can never succeed. No test catches it: `offline-copy-recovery.test.ts` mocks `@/api/documents` `createDocument` wholesale, and `offline-runtime.test.tsx` mocks `recoverOfflineCopy`. (The other two no-workspace callers, `document-list.tsx:420` and `upload-queue.ts:234`, are conditional fallbacks; this new call site is unconditional.)

samples.summary: `collectStale` sweeps every account's entries and archives, but the liveness guard it consults is scoped to the signed-in user, so another account's entry can be deleted out from under a live client in another tab
samples.evidence: `collectStale` deliberately collects aged headers for all users (`headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)`, line 1167) and drops all users' archives (`dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)`, line 1190). The only protection for an open document is `await this.isLive(docKey)` (line 1170), which falls through to the injected `isOpenElsewhere`; `OfflineRuntime` injects `isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:74-75), which matches only lock names prefixed `wb-durable:{thisUserId}:` (durable-session.ts `isOpenInAnyTab`). So for another account's entry the guard answers `false` by construction, and `whenUnknown:false` also removes the guard entirely on a browser without `locks.query`. The victim's `evicted` marker is per-tab module state (`evictedKeys` in wafflebase-doc-store.ts), so the other tab's client never learns and its appends are taken for the contract's silent "no base" success — the exact silent-append loss every other delete path is careful to avoid. Reach is limited because `load()` calls `touch()`, so an entry open in another tab is normally not 30 days stale.

samples.summary: Re-opening the same document can lose its own election: the Web Lock release settles asynchronously, so the remount's `ifAvailable` request is refused by this tab's just-released lock and nothing retries
samples.evidence: `acquireDurableSession` deletes the shared `elections` entry and calls `releaseLock()` synchronously on the last release, but with the real adapter (`webLocks()`), releasing only resolves the parked callback promise — the browser frees the name a turn of the loop later (the suite acknowledges this: durable-session.test.ts `flush()` before asserting `locks.held.size === 0`). On an unmount/remount of the same document (route re-entry, a `key` change), `useDurableDocument`'s cleanup releases and the new effect immediately issues `request(name, {ifAvailable:true})`, which can still see the name held and resolve `undefined` (use-durable-document.ts:205). `decision` is then latched as non-durable for that subject and the effect's dependencies never change, so nothing retries: the document silently runs non-durable for the whole open even though no other tab exists. Same class of bug the in-tab `elections` map was added to fix, but across the unmount boundary.

samples.summary: The unmount cleanup closes the store while its async work may still be running, and the recovery toast outlives the component — both re-open an IndexedDB connection that is then never closed
samples.evidence: The effect cleanup sets `cancelled = true` and calls `store.close()` (line 195), but the IIFE started at line 92 may be inside `store.collectStale()` or `offerRecoverableWork`; `close()` only clears `this.db`/`this.opening`, so the next `this.open()` inside that in-flight work opens a fresh connection with nothing left to close it. The same is true of the `Save a copy` handler: the toast is `duration: Infinity` and `<Toaster/>` is mounted outside the router, so `recoverOfflineCopy(store, ...)` (line 253) runs against a store whose owner unmounted, re-opening the database permanently. A lingering connection blocks another tab's `versionchange`/`deleteDatabase` until `db.onversionchange` fires, and leaks a handle per navigation out of the authenticated shell.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end in the repo. `recoverOfflineCopy` calls `createDocument({ title, type })` unconditionally at offline-copy-recovery.ts:196 and :210, and its signature (:175-179) has no workspace parameter; the only production caller (offline-runtime.tsx:253-256) passes just `{title, type}`. `api/documents.ts:11-29` POSTs that body verbatim to `${API}/documents` — its payload type does not even accept `workspaceId` — and `fetchWithAuth` (api/auth.ts:238-253) adds nothing to the body. The single backend `@Post('documents')` (document.controller.ts:197-200) binds `CreateDocumentInWorkspaceDto`, whose `workspaceId` is `@IsUUID()` with no `@IsOptional()` (document.dto.ts:84-85), under a global `ValidationPipe({whitelist:true, forbidNonWhitelisted:true})` (main.ts:73-80), so the request 400s before the handler (which dereferences `body.workspaceId` at controller.ts:203). `assertOk` then throws and offline-runtime.tsx:285-288 swallows it into a generic toast, so the 'Save a copy' recovery action can never succeed — a core flow of the feature is broken on the normal path. No guard, default-workspace fallback, or alternate route exists; the other two no-workspace callers (document-list.tsx:415-420, upload-queue.ts:233-234) are ternary fallbacks and do not protect this call site.
